title: Ocean Warming Effects on Catch and Revenue Composition in the Northwestern Mediterranean Sea
content:
Climate change-driven ocean warming is affecting marine fisheries in the Northwestern Mediterranean, with implications for both fishing catch and revenue composition. Analyzing 23 years of commercial landings, warmer-water species have become more abundant and contributed more to fishing revenues, while colder-water species have declined and contributed less to fishing revenues. This shift is happening across different taxonomic groups, fleets, and fishing harbors. These changes highlight the need for better management to help fishermen adapt to both the ecological and economic challenges posed by climate change.


ABSTRACT

Climate change-induced ocean warming can have profound implications for marine ecosystems and the socioeconomic activities dependent on them, affecting the catch composition, and fisheries revenue. Our study evaluates spatio-temporal changes in the Northwestern Mediterranean marine fisheries catch and revenue composition tied to ocean warming and disentangles the different underlying processes. To do so, we analyzed the weighted mean thermal affinity of the catch (Mean Temperature of the Catch: MTC) and revenue (Mean Temperature of Revenue: MTR) across different taxonomic groups, fishing fleets, and fishing harbors, using a 23-year time series of commercial landings. Results revealed changes in catch and revenue composition, with an overall temporal increase in the MTC (0.68°C per decade) and MTR (0.58°C per decade) linked to local sea temperature. The temporal increase in both indices prevailed across fishing fleets and taxonomic groups. The processes underpinning these changes over time were tropicalization (i.e. relative increase of warm-affinity species; 41.97% for MTC and 45.20% for MTR), and deborealization (i.e. relative decrease of cold-affinity species; 46.58% for MTC and 44.99% for MTR), with variability across dimensions. Deborealization particularly influenced pelagic fisheries (i.e. purse-seiners and surface longliners) and some commercially important species (e.g. European hake, blue whiting, and Norway lobster). Even if the temporal increase in MTC and MTR was consistent across taxonomic groups and fleets, the spatial dimension showed heterogeneity and temporal declines in some cases. In summary, our study provides valuable information about temporal changes in catch composition associated with local ocean warming and reveals potential cascading effects through the social-ecological system. In particular, we presented the MTR approach for the first time, evidencing ocean warming effects on revenue composition. We suggest that the correlation between changes in catch and revenue composition reveals the adaptive capacity, or fragility of specific fishing fleets and points to management priorities.

ABSTRACT

O quecemento dos océanos inducido polo cambio climático pode ter profundas implicacións para os ecosistemas mariños e as actividades socioeconómicas dependentes deles, afectando á composición das capturas e os ingresos da pesca. O noso estudo avalía os cambios espazo-temporais na composición das capturas e dos ingresos pesqueiros do Mediterráneo noroccidental asociados ao quecemento dos océanos e desentraña os diferentes procesos subxacentes. Para iso, analizamos a afinidade térmica media ponderada das capturas (Temperatura Media das Capturas: MTC) e dos ingresos (Temperatura Media dos Ingresos: MTR) entre diferentes grupos taxonómicos, frotas pesqueiras e portos pesqueiros, empregando unha serie temporal de 23 anos de desembarques comerciais. Os resultados revelaron cambios na composición das capturas e dos ingresos, cun aumento temporal xeral do MTC (0.68°C por década) e do MTR (0.58°C por década) ligados á temperatura local do mar. O aumento temporal en ambos índices prevaleceu en todas as frotas pesqueiras e grupos taxonómicos. Os procesos que sustentan estes cambios ao longo do tempo foron a tropicalización (é dicir, aumento relativo de especies con afinidade cálida; 41.97% para a MTC e 45.20% para a MTR), e a deborealización (é dicir, diminución relativa de especies con afinidade fría; 46.58% para a MTC e 44.99% para a MTR), con variabilidade entre dimensións. A deborealización influíu especialmente nas frotas pesqueiras peláxicas (é dicir, cerqueiros e palangreiros de superficie) e nalgunhas especies de importancia comercial (por exemplo, a merluza, o lirio e a cigala). Aínda que o aumento temporal no MTC e no MTR foi consistente entre os grupos taxonómicos e as frotas, a dimensión espacial mostrou heteroxeneidade e descensos temporais nalgúns casos. En resumo, o noso estudo achega información valiosa sobre os cambios temporais na composición das capturas asociados ao quecemento local do océano e revela potenciais efectos en cascada a través do sistema socioecolóxico. En particular, presentamos por primeira vez o enfoque MTR, evidenciando os efectos do quecemento dos océanos na composición dos ingresos. Suxerimos que a correlación entre os cambios na composición das capturas e dos ingresos revela a capacidade adaptativa ou a fraxilidade de frotas pesqueiras específicas e sinala prioridades de xestión.
